title: The frame shown at a whole second is the one that starts there
goal: Asked for the picture at exactly 10 seconds, the app shows the frame that ends at 10 seconds rather than the one that begins there, one frame early. The canvas, a video export and the agent tools all use the same frames, so an edit placed at a whole second can show a frame a person did not expect.
notes: Found 2026-10-19 by an agent session in the try path of an-agent-can-reach-the-running-app-read-the-open (transcript: queue/audits/2026-10-19-agent-mcp-transcript.md). Reproduction: a 30 fps test recording made with `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=1280x800:rate=30:duration=15 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p "Demo recording.mp4"`; the agent tool video_frame at seconds 10 and 10.02 both drew the frame stamped 00:00:09.967 (frame 299), and 10.04 drew 00:00:10.000 (frame 300). video_frame draws through DocumentFrames, the video export path. Cause, read in code not proven: MovieRef.frameStepMS is 33 (MovieClip.swift:36) and frameIndex(atSourceMS:) is ms / 33, so 10000 ms -> index 303 -> 9999 ms, which the decoder resolves to the frame before 10.000. A 33 ms grid against 33.33 ms frames lands just short of every whole second. Check whether the decoder takes the frame AT or BEFORE the asked moment before changing the grid.
acceptance: On a 30 fps recording whose frames carry their own timecode, the frame drawn at 10.000 s is frame 300 (stamped 00:00:10.000), checked by a test against a real decode
The same holds at 1 s, 60 s and 600 s, so the error does not grow with length
Export and the canvas still agree frame for frame
